decisions.head: малтай
decisions.evidence: Pass-1 doubt (ичи or нчи) re-checked at zoom 8 and on the raw scan bitmap (x 0.465-0.490, y 0.846). The first letter is pixel-for-pixel identical (14x17 px, 0 px difference) to 27 other bold letters on p. 458: 12 of them are и (тейриси x2, минъ, билир x2, тиширыў x2, чибин x2, билимли, -мальдир, эдиле) and 15 are н (аны, къумачны, малгъунлукъ, мальтинлик, малхуння, мамонт, кюннъе, гырджын, ~ны, джаўну, маллыгъын, отунчугъа, бакъгъан, джерине x2). The scan's compression stores bold и and н as one shared shape, so no zoom can tell them apart here. The bar that looked like н carries no information. The third letter is a clearly different и with a visible diagonal. The tie is broken by language: ичи 'its inside' (ич + -и) is a real Karachay-Balkar form, and no Karachay-Balkar word can begin with нч-. Both readers chose ичи. Other sources: the rhyme (малтай / болтай / чыкъ Тотай) occurs nowhere else. 06_lextagged has only this КБРС entry (misc1 'ичи'). rus_kb_dict_33040 has none of these words. In the text layers малтай- appears only as forms of the verb малта- 'trample', and Тотай only as a personal name, a place name or the Virgo constellation (text/05, 23, 43, 50).

decisions.head: малтамакълыкъ
decisions.evidence: zoom 8 (local/s17_img2/zoom/adj458_*.png) and the native 1-bit scan pixels: the end of this line lies on the squeezed/thinned right edge of the right column, so its last letters are narrow and broken but countable; р-у-б-к are clear and the 5th letter is a narrow а (right stem + small lower bowl). рубка is the noun for рубить (малтаргъа 1) рубить). Pass-2 [?] only. Both passes have the same text.

The label pairs with '1) карач.' at the start of the article. The meaning fits: ТСКБЯ малта = 'Топтать кого-что' (06_lextagged, def2) = теплерге. Pass-2 [?] only.

decisions.head: малташыргъа
decisions.evidence: zoom 8 (local/s17_img2/zoom/adj458_*.png) and the native 1-bit scan pixels: the end of this line lies on the squeezed/thinned right edge of the right column, so its last letters are narrow and broken but countable; the bold м-а-л-т-а-р-г are clear and are followed by two narrow broken letters, ъ and а. The reference target is the verb малтаргъа (the article two entries above; малташыргъа is its reciprocal). Pass-2 [?] only.

decisions.head: малхуння

decisions.head: малчы
decisions.evidence: zoom 8 (local/s17_img2/zoom/adj458_*.png) and the native 1-bit scan pixels: the end of this line lies on the squeezed/thinned right edge of the right column, so its last letters are narrow and broken but countable; пасту (with a stress mark) is clear, then three narrow letters ш-и-й with a breve over the last one. There is no descender, so it is not щ. пастуший follows пастушеский as its synonym. Pass-2 [?] only.

decisions.head: малчы
decisions.evidence: zoom 8 (local/s17_img2/zoom/adj458_*.png) and the native 1-bit scan pixels: the end of this line lies on the squeezed/thinned right edge of the right column, so its last letters are narrow and broken but countable; пасту (with a stress mark) is clear, then the narrow ш, ь and я (the я has a diagonal leg). The feminine form agrees with палка. Pass-2 [?] only.

notes: Both passes read p. 458 identically: 41 articles, 0 differences once [?] marks are ignored. I re-checked the pass-1 doubt and the 6 pass-2 [?] marks on the squeezed right edge: all confirm the shared text, and малтай 'ичи' was decided by language, because this scan stores bold и and н as one identical bitmap (28 copies on the page: 12 и, 15 н and the disputed letter).
